title: Global classical solutions of the spatially inhomogeneous Landau–Coulomb equation
decision_reason: Source-backed nice-data continuation question passed recent-theorem comparisons, independent status corroboration, baseline duplicate review and separated adversarial review.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Nonnegative one-species density f(t,x,v); classical anisotropic Landau collision integral with no force term
problem_fingerprint.dimension: Three space and three velocity dimensions
problem_fingerprint.domain: T^3=(R/Z)^3 in x; R^3 in v
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: C-infinity initial data, every x/v derivative rapidly decreasing in v uniformly in x; f0>=delta on |v|<=r for some delta,r>0
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Every admissible f0; every finite T and velocity weight m>=0
problem_fingerprint.normalization: a(z)=|z|^(-1)(I-z tensor z/|z|^2); collision prefactor one; no prescribed total mass
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Global nonnegative solution, smooth for t>0, continuous at t=0 and sup_[0,T] ||<v>^m f||_infinity finite
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Global continuation; no homogeneous, grazing, semiclassical or small-data limit
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Maximal classical existence time is infinity
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Unconditional PDE question; no assumed hydrodynamic bounds

statement_source_and_scope_match: HST Theorems 1.2–1.4 supply the local class and uniqueness, including periodic data. GHS Theorem 1.3 explicitly includes T^3 and gamma=-3 and leaves global continuation unresolved. Nice arbitrary-size data are a standard precise subcase, not a conjecture about every weak solution.
proposed_statement_text: For every smooth, nonnegative, velocity-Schwartz initial density on T^3 x R^3, uniformly positive on a fixed velocity ball, does the local classical Landau solution with Coulomb kernel extend for all positive times with every polynomially weighted L-infinity norm finite on each finite time interval?
applied_significance: The Coulomb operator models collisional redistribution of charged-particle velocities in a plasma. Global classical continuation determines whether a smooth kinetic density remains a valid description at every finite time far from equilibrium.

open_status_evidence_summary: HST and GHS explicitly identify large-data inhomogeneous global regularity as unresolved. Independent SS repeats that status in its February 2026 accepted version. Recent homogeneous, quantum and modified-operator results have different hypotheses.
independent_status_corroboration: SS has no authors in common with GHS; both explicitly discuss the unresolved classical large-data inhomogeneous problem. HST and SS overlap, so that pair alone is not treated as independent.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: Local classical existence and uniqueness for the stated nice data; global perturbative solutions and homogeneous solutions. Continuation criteria require bounds not yet proved for arbitrary inhomogeneous data.
